Fox’s Bug Detective Worksheet for Age 4

Age 4 YearsClass 31 · ScienceType Printable PDFPlays with <a href="/preschool/science/adventures/foxes-bug-detective/">the online game</a>

Six creepy-crawlies and one rule — count the legs and circle every true insect.

On the sheet: Count the legs. Circle the insects!

THE ACTUAL WORKSHEET

Exactly what you’ll print.

This is the real sheet — the same file the buttons above hand you. Title, instructions, the activity itself, and a grown-up answer line where it helps.

Download Free Worksheet ↓ Play This Activity Online ↗

The PDF is a real printable file (A4, prints fine on US Letter). The print button prints only the worksheet — never the website around it. No sign-up, nothing stored.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Counting legs to classify is genuine taxonomy: six legs means insect, eight means spider, none means something else entirely. The rule is checkable by pointing and counting, so every answer can be PROVED on the sheet.

  • Counting to 8
  • The insect rule (six legs)
  • Classifying by a rule
  • Explaining why not
HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. Predict out loud first

    Ask “what do YOU think will happen?” BEFORE any marking begins. A wrong prediction is not a failure — it is the experiment starting.

  2. Point, then mark

    Every answer on these sheets can be pointed at in the picture first. Pointing is thinking made visible — let the finger lead the pencil.

  3. Run the real version

    Each sheet has a real experiment hiding in it: float a spoon, melt an ice cube, blow a dandelion. The worksheet is the invitation, the kitchen is the lab.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Say the WHY

“The metal sinks BECAUSE…” — the explaining is where the science lives. Accept any reasoning that is trying honestly.

Wrong answers are data

Scientists love surprises. “The cork floated — I thought it would sink!” is a genuine discovery worth circling twice.

Keep it short and hands-on

Five minutes of marking plus five minutes of real splashing beats a half hour of paper. One sheet, one experiment, one happy scientist.

Answer guide

Insects (six legs): butterfly, ladybug, ant. Not insects: spider (eight legs), snail (no legs), earthworm (no legs).
